author: Cooper Fox
title: Applying For The Corporal Eugene Cole Scholarship In Maine - NewsBreak
text:
By Cooper Fox ,
7 hours ago
According to WABI , applications are now being accepted for a scholarship established to honor Somerset County Sheriff’s Corporal Eugene Cole, who was killed in the line of duty in Norridgewock on April 25, 2018.
Created in 2019, the Corporal Eugene Cole Scholarship Fund was launched by Cole’s family along with members of the law enforcement community.
Organizers say the goal is to carry forward Cole’s dedication to public service by helping others pursue similar careers.
According to those behind the fund, the scholarship—valued at more than $5,000—is open to Maine residents who are working toward post-secondary education in law enforcement or public safety fields.
They note that eligible career paths include roles such as police work, forensic science, crime or accident reconstruction, cybercrime investigation, and criminal justice, among others.
Fund representatives emphasize that the opportunity is not limited to traditional students. Adults returning to school with plans to enter the law enforcement field are also encouraged to apply, as part of the broader mission to support and grow the next generation of public safety professionals.

These Are the Safest Towns in Maine in 2026 According to research done by Safewise , these are the safest towns and cities in Maine in 2026 #10 - York The small, coastal Maine town has a population of 14,249. #9 - Bar Harbor A tourist hotspot for over 100 years, Bar Harbor has a year round population of only 7,500. #8 - South Berwick Tucked along the Salmon Falls River, South Berwick, Maine feels like a postcard that decided to stay real, blending historic New England charm with a quietly vibrant community spirit. From tree-lined streets and classic homes to its close-knit downtown, it’s the kind of place where small-town warmth still shows up daily and somehow never gets old. #7 - Gorham Home to a branch of the University of Southern Maine, the town has a population of just over 18,000 people. #6 - Hampden Hampden, Maine sits just outside Bangor and strikes that perfect balance between peaceful, small-town living and easy access to everything you need. With its strong sense of community, scenic spots along the Penobscot River, and a pace that lets you actually breathe, Hampden feels like the kind of place people move to and stay put. #5 - Belfast With a population of 7,111, Belfast, is a vibrant coastal town where working waterfront grit meets an artsy, creative heartbeat along the shores of Penobscot Bay. With its walkable downtown, colorful shops, and front-row views of the ocean, it’s the kind of place that feels both timeless and quietly buzzing at the same time. #4 - Orono Like the other college towns on the list, Orono has very little crime. And, the town of just over 12,000 has almost no instances of violent crime. #3 - Cape Elizabeth With a population of just over 9,600, the affluent "bedroom Portland" community has very little crime. #2 - Cumberland Cumberland, Maine, is a picturesque town just north of Portland, known for its quiet neighborhoods and scenic lakes like Highland and Sebago. With a strong sense of community, great schools, and easy access to outdoor activities, it’s a favorite for families and those seeking a peaceful, small-town feel not far from the city. The town reported NO violent crime in the last twelve months! #1 - Eliot Eliot is a town in York County that was first settled in 1623 and was once part of neighboring Kittery. It’s the second-most southern town in the state, sitting along the Piscataqua River directly across from Portsmouth and Newington, New Hampshire. The town has not had one reported violent crime in the last year.
